label: paragraph_title
text: Spirit of Unity.

label: text
text: Marshal von Hindenburg, in pursuance of his presidential candidature, this evening received a number of German and foreign journalists.

label: text
text: He read out to them in a vigorous, clear voice a statement of which the theme was the need for restoration for peaceful labour of that spirit of unity which characterized Germany in the war. This would be a unity not concerned with Party politics but an outcome of wholesome feeling.

label: text
text: As President of the Reich he would only think of his duty and strive for the best interests of the Fatherland on the basis of the constitution and Germany's present position in the world.

label: text
text: He asked them not to expect from him the programme of a Party man who, entered into detailed political issues. The most important consideration was to restore German prestige in the world.

label: text
text: Nothing was more capable of jocopardizing the peaceful object of the restoration of the Fatherland and collaboration in the progress of the world than blatant falsehoods about a threatening German military reaction having inspired his candidature.

label: text
text: He emphasised that he was only striving “to ensure German sovereignty and freedom with a place in the sun of the nations.”

label: text
text: "To attain this the grave charge of our war guilt must be dropped. You will surely believe all this prattle about my unconstitutional plans and reactionary and other dangerous machinations is senseless."

label: text
text: The address was frequently interrupted by shouts of “Bravo!” and enthusiastic cheering, especially at the reference to war guilt.

label: text

It is significant, however, that the prospects of German trade have recently been he dominating note on the campaign, the Marxites using the recent slump in the foreign loan market as an argument against the Nationalists, and the latter labelling Marx as anti-capitalist candidate on count of his Socialist support. The electors are confronted with a bewildering mass of trade statistics, constituting the chief material argument of envir side that its candidate alone is likely to attract foreign capital.

label: text
text: Addressing an audience of twenty thousand, Dr. Marx said that Germany must make sacrifices in order to maintain peace and secure the western frontier. Nevertheless, the Franco-German understanding was a valuable political aim, but acceptance of the security practices regards the west afforded all the more reason why Germany must remember the unntural frontier conditions in the east and the social affinity binding them to Austria. Germany must again put forward a claim for national union with Austria and the resurrection of the Great Germany.

label: paragraph_title
text: FRANCE'S POLITICS

label: paragraph_title
text: (Reuter's Service.)

label: paragraph_title
text: Paris, April 18.

label: text
text: With not a single member of M. Herriot's Cabinet remaining in office, and with five Senators appointed Cabinet members, M. Painleve has done his best to placate the Senate, which brought down M. Herriot. The question remains whether the Senate, which sentenced M. Caillaux, will tolerate a Cabinet wherein M. Caillaux is a dominating factor. The Senate at the moment seems inclined to bury the hatchet, probably on account of M. Caillaux's well-known aversion to a capital levy. A likelier contingency is a split in the Left Cartel, that strange alliance of Radicals and Socialists, for M. Briand is opposed to abolition of the Empassy to the Vatican which is one of the chief points in the Cartel's programme.

label: text
text: The question as to whether the Socialists will support a Cabinet which rejects the capital levy is temporarily settled, for the socialist leaders, after conferring with M. Painleve to-day announced that a broad agreement was reached that the Ministerial declaration should be based on the same principles as inspired the Herriot Government.

label: text
text: M. Briand's tactical talents have full scope in smoothing the relations of the two chambers, failure to improve which may mean that a dissolution will be inevitable; but M. Painleve's mathematics are likely to be taxed in solving the personal equation of antagonism between M. Briand and M. Caillaux.

label: text
text: The dominating factor remains finance, "whereanent public anxiety is such that even the bitterest opponents of M. Caillaux are resigned to swallowing the pills of his political revival, for almost mystic store is set upon his financial technique and strength of purpose.

Peking, April 19.—The Reorganisation Conference disposed of the remaining agenda items yesterday, including the regulations for the national delegates' conference, which were approved. The Conference again meets to-marrow to discuss the financial rehabilitation proposals, and the closing session takes place on Tuesday.—Courtesy of the "Daily Bulletin."
NIGERIA INCIDENTS.

label: text
text: HIS ROYAL HIGHNESS AT POLO.

label: text
text: (Reuter's Service.)

label: text
text:
The Prince of Wales left Kano this morning enroute for Lagos. His first destination is Jbadan.
The Prince has clearly benefited from the polo yesterday, which was his first ride since March 28.
The intense heat has slightly affected some members of the Prince's staff, though in noise seriously.

label: text
text: [Ibadan is a town in the west province of Southern Nigeria, capital of the Yoruba states. It is 12 miles from Lagos. The town has a British President and is a station for Hausa troops. Silk is made at Ibadan and cotton is grown in the vicinity. There is a market for cotton there too. The population is 175,000.]

label: text
text: EARLIFR CAELES

label: text
text: Kano. Nigeria. April 18

label: text
text: Despite the long railway journey here, the Prince of Wales played tennis this evening and after dinner attended an open air dance which was a "veritable fairyland, illuminated with myriads of-coloured lights under the star, sprinkled African sky. The whole floor was specially converted from wild bush two miles from Kano in a space of six weeks.

label: text
text: Though only 130 white people are resident in Kano, five hundred whites attended the dance, mostly uniformed officials from all ports of the Northern Territory. The guests included twenty-five European ladies, charringly dressed, nineteen of whom travelled enormous distances. The Prince shook hands with all and danced practically every dance.

label: paragraph_title
text: THE DURBAR.

label: text
text: The Emir's had already congregated for the Durbar. Most of them travelled hundreds of miles accompanied by hosts of retainers, many of whom died from the intense heat, disease and jungle accidents en route.

label: text
text: Crowds were swarming to Kano all night blowing horns and displaying sleep-destroying enthusiasm. The scenes, this morning were amazing. Streams of plodding visitors were visible on all the roads for miles, resembling converging armies of ants.

label: text
text: At the Durbar at 8 o'clock this morning there was a wonderful cavalry display. It was a case of horses everywhere. Twenty thousand were ranged in horse-shoe formation, all flaunting the gayest colours, and with British officers galloping about completing arrangements.

label: text
text:
The commotion was hushed upon the arrival of the Prince of Wales, the complete silence being the Hansa token of respect. Then the band of the Nigerian Regiment crashed into a stirring march, followed by the rolling of hundreds of native drums.
The Prince was seated on a dais covered with a multi-coloured canopy captured in fighting seventy years ago. His Royal Highness watched the parade, first the infantry and artillery, the latter carrying the gunparts on their heads. Then the Emirs' troopers charged with lances and swords drawn, halting spectacularly two feet from the dais. The cavalry thereafter marched past headed by bands playing ancient instruments, all clad in gorgeous uniforms. The concourse of spectators, whose blood was fired by the continuous roll of exultant drums, cheered tumultuously.

label: paragraph_title
text: DEVIL DANCERS.

label: text
text: Numerous riders were accounted in the old-time uniform of Crusaders or in chain mail complete with visor, and added a bizarre touch to the dazzling scene. Outbursts of frenzied cheering rent the air as the dense columns filed past the dais to the accompaniment of deafening drums.

label: text
text: Interspersed between files of cavalry at the walk appeared groups of dancers, wildly gyrating and snouting. They were perfect types of devil dancers.

label: text
text: Every moment saw something fresh in the never-ending procession—brilliant all red uniforms, golden bows and arrows, five-foot trumpets, plumed helmets and finally a most magnificent body of Bornu Cavalry, with heads befeathered, rode waving cutlasses and swords; accompanied by a special troop mounted on beautifully caparisoned camels and carrying enormous silk flags.

label: text
text:
The scene was staggering, thousands of superb horsemen standing in their stirrups, shrieking waving their swords and bouncing in their saddles. It was truly an orgy of colour.

label: text
text: (Sofia, April 19.)

label: text
text: Captain Krtoneff, who is alleged to have procured the explosives used in the Cathedral, has committed suicide. His wife is said to have been killed by the Communists in order to prevent her from revealing the plot.

label: text
text: A Cathedral servant has been arrested. It is alleged he was bribed to permit a man to place the infernal machine in position.

label: text
text: The British members of Parliament," Messrs. J. Wedgewood (Labour), P. B. Malone (Conservative) and W. MacKinder (Labour) have arrived in Sofia to study the situation.

label: text
text: The War Minister, in an interview, declared an increase in the army was indispensable to maintain order. Steps would be taken to conscript an additional $10,000 men.

label: text
text:
Conspirators Arrested?
Paris, April 19

label: text
text: A message from Sofia states that the police have discovered the authors of the Cathedral outrage. They are alleged to be Yankoff and Minkoff, President and Vice-President, respectively, of the Central Communist Committee. Almost all the Communist leaders have been arrested.

label: paragraph_title
text: Earlier Cables.

label: text
text: One of the three domes of the Sveta Nedelia Cathedral, where the infernal machine was deposited, has completely collapsed, also the south porch, while there is grave danger of the central Dome collapsing.

label: text
text: The whole town is mourning and all shops are shut.

label: paragraph_title
text: RHESUS IN PORT.

label: paragraph_title
text: (Reuter's Service.)

label: paragraph_title
text: Port Said, April 19.

label: text
text: The steamer Rhesus has arrived here towed by another vessel. She will discharge her cargo then go to Alexandria for dry dock repairs, after which she is expected to return here to reload.

label: text
text: The final list of Cathedral victims includes thirteen Generals, three Deputies, the Mayor of Sofia, eight high Government officials, two lawyers, nineteen women and seven children. All the victims were buried in the same grave after a funeral service in the cemetery. One of the bell-ringers of the Cathedral is among those arrested on suspicion.

label: text
text: The parade closed with gallops past by detachments, a fitting finish to a wondrous demonstration of loyalty never seen before and never to be seen again. The spectators were entranced.

label: text
text:
A reception to the Emirs followed, the latter squatting in a semi-circle fully fifty yards from the Prince to hear his address. The official interpreter was standing near the Prince, and the latter, remarking that the Emirs were unable to hear, motioned them to approach, whereafter they squatted at the foot of the dais:
The Minister for the Interior, interviewed, said the Agrarian Communist party had sold itself to foreign interests. The arrested criminal members of the party had made disclosures which made the discovery of the authors of the outrage possible.

label: text
text: The Premier declared the Government's determination to repress Communist and Anarchists' attempts. The Government is introducing a Bill to provide grants for the families bereaved by the explosion.

label: text
text: FORMER CROWN PRINCE EXONERATED.

label: text
text: GERMAN COURT'S FINDING.

label: text
text:
(Ietter's Service.)
Berlin April 19

label: text
text: cluded its investigation into the alleged war crimes of the former Crown Prince.

label: text
text: The court has found that the Crown Prince never ordered the burning and plundering of villages and towns. He was not responsible for the executions ordered by the military tribunals of his army corps.

label: text
text: Therefore the court quashed further proceedings.

label: text
text: Marshall van Hindenburg, replying to a questionnaire submitted by Reuter's correspondent, said that if he were chosen President he would respect the military as well as the other provisions of the Versailles treaty. His outlook was a peaceful one.

label: text
text: He was convinced that it would be foolish for Germany to indulge in warlike adventures which after the war he had always opposed because they could only end disastrously.

label: text
text: As a military expert he did not think Germany was even capable of defending herself against the small neighbouring states. Poland and Czecho-Slovakia possessed bigger standing armies, and were protected by the military alliances.

label: text
text: Paris, April 18.—It is learned authoritatively that the Peking report of settlement of the controversy re the French share of the Boxer Indemnity is premature in the form wherein it was published, but an agreement equally satisfactory to the two countries is well within sight.—Havas.

label: text
text: PROPOSED BORDER FENCE—The suggestion has been made to Congress that a barbed wire fence, 18 feet high and 30 miles long, be erected along the Main can border east of El Faso to prevent smuggling of liqueur and aliens. It would resemble that on the California border.
